root_cause.text: In GFS2’s `gfs2_fill_super()`/`gfs2_make_fs_rw()` control flow, error handling failed to clean up resources on two specific paths: the `fail_per_node` label skipped `gfs2_destroy_threads()` after `init_threads()` created `logd`/`quotad`, and `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` did not call `gfs2_quota_cleanup()` when quota init succeeded but the filesystem was then withdrawn and returned `-EIO`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp);` from the `gfs2_fill_super()` error block and adds it at `fail_per_node`, showing the thread cleanup was missing on that path; it also adds `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp);` in `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` specifically when `gfs2_quota_init(sdp)` succeeds and `gfs2_withdrawn(sdp)` is true, confirming the quota bitmap leak occurred in that withdrawal-after-init case.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The GFS2 mount/read-write transition error paths failed to unwind partially initialized resources correctly, leaving `logd`/`quotad` kthreads and the quota bitmap allocated when `gfs2_freeze_lock_shared()` or `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` returned an error.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp)` from the `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` error block and adds it unconditionally to `fail_per_node` in `fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c`, and it adds `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp)` in `fs/gfs2/super.c` when `gfs2_quota_init(sdp)` succeeds but `gfs2_withdrawn(sdp)` causes `-EIO`, matching the leak backtraces from `init_threads()`/`gfs2_quota_init()`.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence supports two specific leaks, but the proposed root cause is too broad and partly inconsistent. The patch/CVE describe leaks in the `gfs2_fill_super()` error path: missing `gfs2_destroy_threads()` on the `fail_per_node` path after `gfs2_freeze_lock_shared()` fails, and missing `gfs2_quota_cleanup()` when `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` succeeds in quota init but then `gfs2_withdrawn(sdp)` causes `-EIO`. The proposed root cause incorrectly attributes the quota leak to `gfs2_freeze_lock_shared()`/`gfs2_make_fs_rw()` error paths generally and mentions “partially initialized resources” without explaining the specific control-flow bug. It also implies leaked `logd`/`quotad` kthreads and quota bitmap when either helper returns an error, whereas the patch only fixes the thread cleanup in the `gfs2_fill_super()` error path and the quota cleanup only for the withdrawn-after-quota-init case.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In GFS2’s `gfs2_fill_super()`/`gfs2_make_fs_rw()` control flow, error handling failed to clean up resources on two specific paths: the `fail_per_node` label skipped `gfs2_destroy_threads()` after `init_threads()` created `logd`/`quotad`, and `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` did not call `gfs2_quota_cleanup()` when quota init succeeded but the filesystem was then withdrawn and returned `-EIO`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp);` from the `gfs2_fill_super()` error block and adds it at `fail_per_node`, showing the thread cleanup was missing on that path; it also adds `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp);` in `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` specifically when `gfs2_quota_init(sdp)` succeeds and `gfs2_withdrawn(sdp)` is true, confirming the quota bitmap leak occurred in that withdrawal-after-init case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature thread destruction from the gfs2_fill_super read-write failure path.
intent_record.what: In the error path inside gfs2_fill_super(), the call to gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp) was removed from the block that handles failure after gfs2_freeze_unlock(sdp) and before logging the "can't make FS RW" error.
intent_record.how: On this failure path, the code now leaves thread teardown to later cleanup instead of destroying GFS2 threads immediately after a failed attempt to make the filesystem read-write. This avoids performing that cleanup too early or redundantly during the superblock setup error handling flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mount failure cleanup by destroying GFS2 threads during the `fail_per_node` error path.
intent_record.what: In the error-handling path labeled `fail_per_node`, a new call to `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp);` was inserted immediately after `init_per_node(sdp, UNDO);` and before the `fail_inodes` label.
intent_record.how: If `gfs2_fill_super()` fails after per-node initialization, it now explicitly tears down GFS2 threads before continuing the rest of the cleanup sequence. This prevents thread resources from being left running or leaked during mount failure cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure quota initialization is cleaned up when GFS2 withdraws during transition to read-write mode.
intent_record.what: The code now wraps the `if (!error && gfs2_withdrawn(sdp))` branch in braces and adds a call to `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp)` before setting `error = -EIO`.
intent_record.how: If quota initialization succeeds but the filesystem has already been withdrawn, the newly initialized quota state is now cleaned up before returning an I/O error, preventing quota resources from დარჩing initialized in a withdrawn failure path.

Fix mount failure cleanup by destroying GFS2 threads during the `fail_per_node` error path.

The change directly matches one of the root-cause cleanup failures: it adds destruction of GFS2 threads on the `fail_per_node` mount-error path, fixing the missing `gfs2_destroy_threads()` cleanup after `init_threads()`.
The group directly matches one of the root-cause cleanup failures: it adds quota cleanup when gfs2_make_fs_rw() succeeds in quota init but the filesystem is withdrawn and returns -EIO.

The fail_per_node cleanup path previously only undid per-node state and skipped thread destruction, leaving threads allocated after init_threads() on mount failure.
This is the quota initialization that can succeed before withdrawal; the vulnerability arises because subsequent withdrawal/EIO handling returned without performing quota cleanup.
This is the specific control-flow condition where GFS2 can become withdrawn after quota init succeeds, triggering the missing cleanup path described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement begins the quota initialization sequence in gfs2_make_fs_rw(). The root cause says that if quota init succeeds and the filesystem is then withdrawn, the old control flow failed to clean up quota resources before returning -EIO.
This is the exact withdrawal check that leads into the missing cleanup path. In the vulnerable version, this branch returned failure without calling gfs2_quota_cleanup() after successful quota init.

This is the fail_per_node cleanup path that, before the fix, only undid per-node state and skipped gfs2_destroy_threads(). The root cause identifies this path as leaking logd/quotad after init_threads() had created them.

The snippet clearly shows both vulnerable control-flow areas. In `fill_super()`, after `init_threads(sdp, DO)` succeeds, the error path goes to `fail_per_node:` for `gfs2_statfs_init()` failures and also for `init_threads()` failures: `if (error) goto fail_per_node;`. This matches the root cause that the `fail_per_node` path skipped thread destruction after `logd`/`quotad` creation.

The second root cause path is not fixed either: the code calls `gfs2_make_fs_rw(sdp);` and on error does `goto fail_threads;` where only `init_threads(sdp, UNDO);` is invoked. There is no visible `gfs2_quota_cleanup()` or quota-specific teardown here before unwinding, so if `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` had initialized quota state and then failed with `-EIO`, the cleanup described in the vulnerability root cause is absent.

Since the shown function body contains the relevant mount/error handling logic and the missing cleanup is directly observable, the code is sufficient to determine the bug is present and the fix is not yet present.
